about: Conduit's rich cards: the one definition both the conduit_push plugin and Conduit read. Conduit ships a byte-identical copy (Conduit/Cards/card-schema.json) and its CI fails when the copy differs from this file on main. 'card' is a JSON Schema subset (type, enum, properties, required, items, minItems, maxItems, maxLength, minimum, maximum, format uri) that goes into the tool definitions as is. Normalizing is the same on both sides: unknown keys are dropped, text is cleaned and cut to maxLength, an invalid optional value is dropped, an invalid list item is dropped, and an invalid required value makes its object invalid. Then the rules in 'rules' apply. cards/card-vectors.json holds the shared examples both test suites run.
rules: A card keeps only its own type's field (places for map, place and places; people for contact; stats, chart, weather, options, steps, media or status for the others), plus title and live, source on every type but map, place and places, and needs on steps; a card without its type's field is dropped.
A route is kept only on a map card, only when every place given survived, when 'to' (and 'from' if given) name places in the list, and when 'from' differs from 'to'.
A place card keeps only its first place.
A place's or person's photo is kept only when its url is https.
A chart keeps only the series with one value per label; a pie keeps only its first series, and no value of a pie may be negative. A chart with no series left is dropped.
A weather card needs a source and at least one of now, hours or days (an empty list counts as none); a day whose low is above its high is dropped.
A comparison keeps only its first recommended option.
A media card needs a source and keeps only items whose url is https (dropped when none is left); artwork is kept only when it is https, and an image keeps no duration or artwork.

A contact's phone is kept only when it holds 3 to 20 digits and nothing but digits, spaces and + - ( ) . characters; an email only when it is one address like name@example.com, with no spaces, quotes, brackets, commas, semicolons, colons or any of ? # % & =.
A person's message is kept only when their phone is.
Only the first card in a set keeps a given live name.

card.description: One card Conduit draws natively. map: a map with a pin per place, and a route when you give one. place: one place in detail. places: several places to swipe through. stats: a few big numbers. chart: a line, bar or pie chart. weather: a forecast. comparison: two to four options side by side. steps: instructions to follow, with timers. media: photos, videos or audio to look at or play. contact: a few people to call, message or email, or someone to text with a message you wrote for the user to send. status: how something in progress is going, like a delivery, a flight, a match or a job.

type.description: The kind of card; fill in its field: places for map, place and places, people for contact, otherwise the field named like the type (options for comparison).

title.description: A short heading, a few words.

live.description: A name for a card you'll keep up to date, like order-4411 or deploy. Show a card with the same live name again in this conversation and it replaces this one wherever it's shown, so give the whole card each time.

source.description: Every type but map, place and places: where the information is from, when it's from a tool, a site or a service rather than your own knowledge. Required for weather and media. Shown on the card.

name.description: Like Open-Meteo, Yahoo Finance or the user's Health data.

places.description: The places, best first. The phone finds each one in Apple Maps itself and shows Apple Maps' address, category, phone, website, travel time and Look Around: don't fill those in. Give coordinates or the place_id from conduit_maps when you have them; otherwise a name and address precise enough to find it.

address.description: Its address or area, to find it.

place_id.description: The Apple Maps place id conduit_maps gave, if any.

note.description: Your own short note on it, shown as yours: why it fits, what to order.

rating.description: Only a rating you actually found, with where it's from. Left out without a source.

source.description: Where it's from, like Google or Yelp.

hours.description: Opening hours you actually found, with where they're from. Left out without a source.

price.description: A price level or price you actually found, with where it's from. Left out without a source.

photo.description: A photo of the place you actually found: a direct image URL, with where it's from. Left out without a source.

route.description: map only: draw a route. Places are counted from 0.

to.description: The place the route goes to.

from.description: The place it starts at. Leave it out to start where the user is.

mode.description: How to travel; driving if left out.

stats.description: stats only: big numbers with labels, most important first.

label.description: What it is, like Steps or Portfolio.

value.description: The number as it should read, with its unit, like 8,412 or $12.4k.

detail.description: A few words under it, like of 10,000 or last 30 days.

tone.description: Whether the change is good news; neutral if left out.

spark.description: Recent values, oldest first, drawn as a small line.

chart.description: chart only: the data, drawn as a native chart.

kind.description: line or area for change over time, bar to compare, pie for shares of a whole.

labels.description: The x-axis labels in order, or a pie's slice names.

series.description: One or more series, each with one value per label. A pie has one.

values.description: One value per label, in order.

unit.description: The values' unit, like %, kg or USD.

weather.description: weather only: a forecast you got from a weather tool or site, never guessed. Give the card's source.

text.description: A few words, like Feels like 21 or Windy later.

precip.description: Chance of rain or snow, in percent.
Chance of rain or snow, in percent.

options.description: comparison only: the options, side by side.

facts.description: Facts to compare, with the same labels in the same order for every option.

pros.description: What's good about it, a few words each.

cons.description: What's not, a few words each.

recommended.description: true on the one you recommend, if any.

needs.description: steps only: what to have ready first, like ingredients or tools.

steps.description: steps only: the steps in order. The user can tick them off.

timer.description: Seconds, when the step waits a set time (simmer 10 minutes is 600): the user can start a timer from it.

media.description: media only: the photos, videos or audio, in order. Only files you actually found, as direct links the phone can load; send a file on this machine as an attachment instead.

url.description: A direct https link to the file or stream (like .jpg, .png, .mp4, .m3u8, .mp3 or .m4a), not a page.

by.description: Who made it: the artist, channel or photographer.

duration.description: video and audio: its length in seconds, if known.

artwork.description: video and audio: a direct link to a still or cover image.

people.description: contact only: the people or businesses. The phone checks each against the user's own contacts and says when one is there; anything else reads as yours.

detail.description: Who they are: a role, a business, or how they're related to the user.

phone.description: A phone number you actually have, with the country code when you know it.

email.description: An email address you actually have.

note.description: Your own short note: why you're showing them.

message.description: A text message you wrote for the user to send them, only when the user asked you to text or message this person. Conduit shows it with a Send text button that opens Messages with it filled in, and the user taps Send there. Needs their phone. It isn't sent until the user taps Send, so never say it was sent.

photo.description: A photo of them you actually found: a direct image URL, with where it's from. Left out without a source; the phone uses the contact's own photo when it has one.

status.description: status only: where something in progress stands. Give it a live name and show it again as it changes.

state.description: Where it stands now, a few words: Out for delivery, Boarding, 2-1 at half time, Building.

phase.description: waiting: not started. active: under way. done: finished. problem: delayed, failed or stuck. active if left out.

progress.description: How far along, from 0 to 1, only when you actually know.

detail.description: A line more: where it is, the score, what's happening.

eta.description: When it should finish or arrive, like 14:20 or in 5 min.

milestones.description: The stages, in order, each done or not yet.

label.description: Like Ordered, Shipped, Out for delivery.
